title: Anduril Employee Share Sale Would Value Defense Tech Startup at $90 Billion
excerpt: The Palmer Luckey-founded company is offering staff $94.80 a share in a $1.3 billion tender — a 48% jump from its $61 billion valuation in May.
body:
• Anduril will let current and former employees sell shares at $94.80 each in a tender offer capped at about $1.3 billion, valuing the defense tech company at roughly $90 billion.
  • The offer opened October 13 and closes November 9, and for the first time extends eligibility to employees in 16 countries.
  • The valuation is up about 48% from the $61 billion Anduril reached in May, when it raised $5 billion in a round led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz.
  • Anduril generated $2.2 billion in revenue in 2025 and recently won a US Navy shipyard contract worth up to $2.9 billion.

Anduril Industries will let employees sell stock through a tender offer that values the defense technology company at roughly $90 billion, the latest sign of investor appetite for the startups challenging America's established weapons makers. Bloomberg first reported the offer, and Anduril confirmed it to CNBC.

The Offer, By the Numbers

Eligible shareholders can sell at $94.80 a share, with total purchases capped at about $1.3 billion. The offer opened on October 13 and is scheduled to close on November 9. Bloomberg reported that employees in 16 countries are eligible to participate — a significant widening from earlier tenders limited to the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia.

https://x.com/StockMKTNewz/status/2110420838482640916

Tender offers of this kind have become the pressure valve of the late-stage startup economy: they give employees liquidity on paper wealth without forcing the company into an initial public offering. Anduril has arranged such sales periodically while remaining private.

A Valuation Climbing at Wartime Speed

The roughly $90 billion figure is a jump of about 48% from May, when Anduril closed a $5 billion funding round that doubled its valuation to $61 billion, in a deal led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz. The company generated $2.2 billion in revenue in 2025, according to reporting on the offer — a real business, but one whose market value now prices in years of steep growth.

Founded in 2017 by Oculus creator Palmer Luckey and others, Anduril builds autonomous aircraft, surveillance systems, augmented-reality headsets and the Lattice AI software that ties them together, and has expanded into underwater vehicles and missile systems. The US Defense Department is among its largest customers. This month the company signed a US Navy shipyard contract worth up to $2.9 billion, and Luckey was named a co-director of Project Meridian, an initiative to develop and scale military capabilities.

Why Defense Tech Is Booming

Anduril's rise tracks a structural shift in Pentagon spending toward autonomous systems, artificial intelligence and military modernisation — and toward vendors who build like software companies rather than traditional contractors. Washington's push to reindustrialise the American military has channelled contracts and political access to a new class of defense founders, with Luckey among those taking advisory roles in the capital.

What to Watch

The tender closes November 9. The open question hanging over the $90 billion mark is the one analysts raised immediately: how much future revenue growth is already reflected in the share price. At roughly 40 times trailing revenue, Anduril is being valued less like a weapons manufacturer and more like a software platform — a bet its contract pipeline now has to justify.
